title: Partner Go-to-Market Technical Playbook — Marketplace Integrations
author: Evelyn Park
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is a single-page reference for Redwood field teams and marketplace partners to accelerate technical onboarding, co-selling, and risk clearance for marketplace integrations. It consolidates positioning and messaging, a short competitive brief, a pitch deck checklist, pricing guidance for partner pilots and marketplace offerings, a compact case study, and a security FAQ aimed at technical reviewers.

Scope: marketplace connectors, managed partner integrations, and ISV co-sell pilots. Not intended for enterprise-only Private deployments (see partner-enterprise-onboarding).

Owner: Go-to-market (technical alliances & solutions).

Contents summary
- Positioning & Messaging (one-liners & rebuttals)
- Competitive brief (3 key competitors and our differentiators)
- Pitch deck checklist (7 slides to prioritize)
- Pricing guidance (pilot, marketplace listing, and resale scenarios)
- Case study: PaymentFlow Inc. (pilot -> production summary)
- Security FAQ for partner prospects (12 prioritized Qs)
- Onboarding checklist (10-step technical flow)
- Escalation & ownership matrix

1) Positioning & Messaging
- Core one-liner for partners: "Redwood Inference provides deterministic, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so your app delivers reliable latency, predictable cost, and enterprise controls — whether you ship from the cloud or inside the customer's network."
- Value prompts for marketplace listings:
  - "Ship faster: pre-packaged runtimes and templated connectors cut integration time to days, not months."
  - "Control costs: automated batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles reduce per-token expense without manual tuning."
  - "Enterprise-ready: SLA-backed Dedicated instances, private VPC options, and audit-grade logs for regulated customers."
- Top 3 buyer statements and rebuttals:
  1. "We’ll just call the big cloud model API — why add another layer?"
     - Rebuttal: "Many customers do during prototyping. At scale they need predictable latency/cost and data isolation; Redwood lets them migrate to Dedicated/private modes without changing your integration or UI."
  2. "Open models are cheaper — why pay for a platform?"
     - Rebuttal: "Open models + Redwood = cheaper and reliable serving. We optimize kernels, manage batching/caching, and provide routing/fallbacks so the Open model savings actually translate to production unit economics."
  3. "We’re concerned about compliance and data residency."
     - Rebuttal: "We offer Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments and KMS/HSM integrations; our audit logging and RBAC meet common regulatory requirements — we’ll include a security addendum in the marketplace contract."

2) Competitive brief (one page summary)
- Competitors covered: Major public LLM APIs, Cloud-managed endpoints, and self-hosted inference runtimes.
- Quick grid (differentiators):
  | Area | Redwood | Public LLM APIs | Cloud Managed Endpoints | Self-hosted Runtimes |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Time to initial value | Fast (hosted API + templates) | Fast | Medium | Slow |
  | Production economics | Cost controls (batching, KV caching) | Limited | Variable | High ops cost |
  | Deployment flexibility | Hosted/Dedicated/Private | Hosted only | Region-limited | Custom |
  | Observability & SLO tooling | Token-level, traceable, rollout controls | Basic metrics | Provider specific | Varies |
  | Enterprise controls (KMS, audit, SLA) | Yes (Private + Dedicated) | Limited | Varies | Possible |
- Messaging takeaway: emphasize predictable economics and unified lifecycle (same API/rollout across modes). For partners, emphasize minimal integration change when customers shift from pilot to Dedicated/private.

3) Pitch deck checklist (minimum viable 7 slides)
1. Title & problem statement (who, what, why now) — include expected latency/cost pain points.
2. Redwood solution (one-liner, modes: hosted/dedicated/private).
3. Integration model for partner (how SDK/connector embeds).
4. Performance & cost proof points (sample p50/p95 latencies, per-token cost delta vs alternative).
5. Security & compliance summary (KMS, VPC, SOC/ISO evidence links).
6. Pricing & pilot mechanics (trial credits, pilot timebox, overage rules).
7. Next steps & contact (technical onboarding owner + AE).

Checklist notes: include screenshots of the Console route dashboards for partners; attach short video walkthrough (3–5 minutes).

4) Pricing guidance (recommended framing for partners)
- Pilot (co-sell): 30–90 day pilot, free trial credit up to $X (configured per partner), and a success metric (ex: 10k requests with p95 < 600ms). Pilot terms: partner pays incremental infra beyond credit at discounted rate.
- Marketplace listing: list hosted SKU with per-token pricing tiers, optional Dedicated add-on (monthly base + committed capacity).
- Revenue share models: typical ranges: 70/30 (partner/platform) for lead & billing handled by partner marketplace, or 85/15 for co-sell where Redwood handles billing and partner drives usage. Final split requires legal review.
- Pricing table (example) :
  | Offering | Unit | Pilot price | Marketplace list | Dedicated (monthly) |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Hosted generation | 1k tokens | $0.20 (credit) | $0.30 | n/a |
  | Embeddings | 1k vectors | $0.10 (credit) | $0.15 | n/a |
  | Dedicated reserved | per GPU-month | n/a | n/a | $3,500 (example) |
Notes: replace $ placeholders with current pricing sheet before sending to partner. Ensure finance approves any deviation from standard revenue share.

5) Case study — PaymentFlow Inc. (short)
- Context: PaymentFlow (mid-market fintech) integrated Redwood via a marketplace connector to enable real-time transaction summarization and noisy-card redaction.
- Pilot outcome (45 days):
  - Integration time: 8 days (connector + SDK)
  - Latency: p95 generation ~420ms with Hosted; moved to Dedicated reduced p95 to 210ms for peak traffic
  - Cost: estimated per-transaction model cost reduced 28% after KV caching and 4-bit quantization profile applied
  - Compliance: migrated to Private VPC for production to satisfy PCI-adjacent controls
- ROI narrative: by reducing fraud analyst time and delivering real-time insights, PaymentFlow projected a 2.6x ROI within 9 months.

6) Security FAQ for partner prospects (top items to hand to technical reviewers)
Format note: keep this as a short appendix in customer-facing materials. Always attach compliance pack when requested.
Q1: Where does data live?
A1: Default: Redwood Hosted in region chosen by customer. Options: Dedicated (isolated tenant on our infra) or Private (customer VPC / on-prem).
Q2: Do you persist prompts & responses?
A2: By default we retain logs for 30 days for debugging. Retention can be configured; for regulated customers we offer no-persist deployment profiles.
Q3: How is encryption handled?
A3: Data in transit: TLS 1.2+. At-rest: AES-256. KMS/HSM available for customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated.
Q4: Can we control model selection and weights?
A4: Customers can pin model versions and choose allowed model catalog entries. For Private deployments, bring-your-own-model is supported with onboarding controls.
Q5: Do you have SOC/ISO certs?
A5: Yes — SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence is available on request (link to compliance pack).
Q6: How are credentials and RBAC handled?
A6: Token-based API keys, fine-grained roles in Console, and SSO (SAML/OIDC). Audit logs capture token usage.
Q7: How do you isolate noisy tenants on Dedicated?
A7: Dedicated pools are per-customer reserved GPU capacity with scheduling isolation and tenant-level SLO enforcement; we maintain per-tenant quotas and overcommit controls.
Q8: What is the incident notification policy for partners?
A8: Partners on paid plans receive incident notifications aligned to SLA; we provide a status page and dedicated Slack/PagerDuty channels for enterprise-tier partners.
Q9: Do you support data residency controls?
A9: Yes — regional hosting and on-prem deliverables; data residency can be mandated in contract.
Q10: Are outputs auditable and reproducible?
A10: We provide request/response logs, prompt sets, and model version metadata; reproducibility depends on deterministic model variant choices and fixed tokenization settings.
Q11: What safeguards exist for PII / sensitive content?
A11: Optional pre-processing hooks (regex/NER filters), content classifiers, and automatic redact rules can be applied at the gateway.
Q12: How is third-party library risk managed?
A12: We maintain a vulnerability scanning cadence for runtime components and publish SBOMs for Private deployments on request.

7) Technical onboarding checklist (10-step)
1. Kickoff: alignment doc, success metrics, and IAM accounts exchanged.
2. Access: issue API keys (scoped) and grant Console viewer role to partner lead.
3. Dev sandbox: provide partner with trial credit and sample dataset.
4. Connector install: share SDK example and one-line integration snippet.
   - Example (curl):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"Summarize transaction"}'
5. Performance baseline: run 1k test requests and capture p50/p95 and token counts.
6. Cost tuning: enable batching (suggested batch size 8–16) and KV caching for prefix-heavy workloads.
7. Security review: exchange compliance pack, validate KMS & VPC needs.
8. Pilot validation: run success criteria tests (latency, quality checks, throughput).
9. Rollout plan: canary 5%, then 25%, 100% with rollback play defined.
10. Handover: AE + Solutions sign off, enable billing, and schedule monthly QBR.

8) Escalation & ownership matrix
- Technical issues (performance/regression): Eng-serving-runtime oncall (pager + eng-platform liaison).
- Security/compliance: Security & compliance lead.
- Contract & pricing exceptions: Finance & Legal with go-to-market approval.
- Escalation steps:
  1. Partner raises via partner-portal -> automatically creates ticket in Zendesk + PagerDuty if SLO breached.
  2. Triage owner acknowledges within 1 business hour.
  3. Route to oncall or security as needed; capture RCA within 72 hours after mitigation.

9) Appendices & assets to attach
- One-page compliance pack (SOC 2 + ISO extracts)
- Example slide deck (editable PPTX) with the 7-slide checklist filled in
- Short screencast (Console onboarding) and SDK snippet library
- Pricing worksheet (spreadsheet with placeholders)

10) Approvals & next steps
- Pre-send checklist: update pricing placeholders with current finance sheet; attach latest compliance pack; confirm partner contact and AE.
- If partner requests custom revenue share or pilot credit > $25k, route to RevOps approval.
- Owner for updates: Evelyn Park (GT M alliances).

Contact & distribution
- Primary contacts: Evelyn Park (evelyn.park@redwood.ai), Marcus Li (marcus.li@redwood.ai)
- Distribution recommended: Partner success, Solutions engineers, Field AEs, Partner PMs.
